# Coffee Grinder

## Setup

I found the zero point by running the burrs closed until they just chirp, then marked that collar position with a pencil line. From there the dial sits at 12 for filter brews, which gives a medium grind that drains in about three and a half minutes in the pour over. Espresso wants 4 and French press around 20. I single dose, weighing 15 g per brew and dropping it straight into the top, so there are no stale beans sitting in the hopper. A quick tap on the counter settles the grounds before I pull the cup out.

## Cleaning

Once a week I brush the chute out with a small nylon brush that lives next to the grinder, and I blow the loose chaff off the top plate. I never wash the burrs with water or detergent; moisture starts rust on the steel. A dry cloth handles the body. Every few months I run a handful of dry rice through on the coarse setting to lift old oils.

## Troubleshooting

A coarse gusher and a fast pour usually mean the setting slipped. If the burrs drift out of alignment after a few years and need a shim kit, that is a workshop job. Static cling in winter is worse with dark roasts, so I tap the catch cup once before I pull it. A buzzing motor that will not turn often means a jammed bean in the chute, which clears with a wooden skewer.
